holidays.name: National Have a Bagel Day
holidays.description: A day devoted to the chewy, boiled-then-baked ring of bread. Toast one, slather it with cream cheese, or pile on lox and call it a day.
holidays.origin: Bagels were popularized in the United States by Jewish immigrants from Eastern Europe, and this unofficial food holiday grew out of the modern calendar of food observances.
holidays.funFact: Traditional bagels are boiled in water before baking, which gives them their signature shiny crust and dense, chewy texture.

holidays.name: International Mountain Day
holidays.description: A United Nations observance that celebrates the world's peaks, highlights their importance to freshwater, biodiversity, and communities, and encourages everyone to appreciate and protect them.
holidays.origin: The UN General Assembly designated December 11 as International Mountain Day in 2003, after the 2002 International Year of Mountains.
holidays.funFact: Mountains cover about a quarter of Earth's land surface and provide fresh water for roughly half of humanity.

holidays.name: National Noodle Ring Day
holidays.description: A nostalgic food observance honoring the noodle ring, a retro dish in which cooked noodles are molded into a ring shape and often filled with creamed vegetables or meats.
holidays.origin: Noodle rings were a popular mid-20th-century home-cooking dish, and the day was added to the calendar of food observances to celebrate this vintage creation.
holidays.funFact: Molded dishes like noodle rings were all the rage in mid-century American cookbooks, right alongside gelatin salads.

holidays.name: UNICEF Day
holidays.description: A day marking the anniversary of the founding of the United Nations Children's Fund, celebrating efforts to protect children's health, education, and rights around the world.
holidays.origin: UNICEF was created by the UN General Assembly on December 11, 1946, to provide emergency food and healthcare to children in countries devastated by World War II.
holidays.funFact: UNICEF was originally called the United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund, and it kept the well-known acronym even after the name was shortened.

holidays.name: Many Moods Day
holidays.description: A day to embrace every mood you have, whether you are cheerful, cranky, sleepy, or somewhere in between, and to show a little patience for everyone else's emotional weather.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance in the calendar of quirky holidays, inviting people to acknowledge that having different moods is perfectly normal.
holidays.funFact: Some people say the day is also a great excuse to wear a mood ring and see if it can keep up with you.
